newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Asset swaps worth at least 13 billion rand had been completed out of approved swaps worth 20 billion rand, according to central Reserve Bank figures.

- Deputy President Thabo Mbeki and Zaire's President Mobuto Sese Seko had agreed on a common approach to the UN mandate for humanitarian relief measures and the deployment of a multinational force in the great lakes region.
- President Nelson Mandela fired a fresh broadside at the media last night when he accused the "white controlled conservative media" of co-opting senior black journalists to do their "dirty work".

- South African Breweries raised attributable earnings 16 percent to 553 million rand in the six months to September -- relying on another strong performance from its domestic and international beer interests to offset the squeeze on margins in its retail business.
- Nigel Bruce resigned as editor of the Financial Mail on Wednesday to become the editor of competing magazine Finance Week.

- A solid performance from the local and international beer operations of South African Breweries helped the company report a beter-than-expected 14 percent increase in earnings to 185.2 cents a share for the six months to September 30 from 162.5 cents in the same period.

- Nigel Bruce, the editor of the Financial Mail for the past 11 years, resigned as editor of the financial weekly and from the Times Media Ltd board on Wednesday after what he called a "disagreement with management" over editorial independence.
- Sea Harvest Corporation Ltd, the fishing company controlled by ICS Holdings, is to sell between 7.5 percent and eight percent of its equity to staff for 46 million rand.
- The rand briefly strengthened to 4.64 rand to the dollar on Wednesday, its best level in 12 trading days, but slipped back by the end of the day.
- The mid-air plane crash over northern India, which killed 351 people on Tuesday night may have been caused by pilot error.
- A Star foreign service journalist is trapped with other foreign journalists in the north-eastern Zaire town of Kisangani, with is being ravaged by retreating Zairian army soldiers.
